title: short-circuit quench and graceful rejoin guard
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: during a recent regional surge we observed rapid short-circuit reopen events which caused a thundering-rejoin effect and amplified downstream capacity spikes. In combination with a rollback path that allowed control-plane rollbacks to previous model variants during partial failover windows, this could cause cascading failures and noisy telemetry. This PR introduces two safety controls: (1) a short-circuit 'quench' that temporarily suppresses reopening of short-circuited routes for a configurable backoff window to allow the system to absorb load, and (2) a graceful-rejoin guard that sequences rejoin attempts with a coordinated quorum check and rollback-safeguard to prevent control-plane initiated rollbacks while a region is in an active failover handoff. Additionally this PR fixes telemetry gaps: circuit state transitions were not being emitted for quench-driven suppressions which impeded post-incident analysis. Changes are designed to be conservative and opt-in by default via runtime config with sane defaults for hosted and dedicated deployments. Checklist: - [x] Quench timer implementation and config - [x] Coordinated graceful-rejoin sequencing and rollback safeguard - [x] Emit circuit transition telemetry for quench and guarded rejoin paths - [x] Unit and e2e tests for noisy reopen scenarios - [x] Documentation and upgrade notes for operators - [x] Perf sanity checks for steady-state overhead

- Introduced short-circuit quench to dampen rapid reopen storms
- Added graceful-rejoin coordinator to sequence rejoin attempts and prevent unsafe rollbacks
